government.narrative:
India is a parliamentary democratic republic with a federal structure.{{7}}{{1}} The President is head of state, and executive power rests with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers, who are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.{{1}}{{7}}

Health care delivery is a state responsibility: 'public health and sanitation; hospitals and dispensaries' is Entry 6 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule.{{1}} Medical education sits on the Concurrent List, where Union law prevails in a conflict.{{1}} The Union shapes the system through money and regulation; the Fifteenth Finance Commission, for example, earmarked about Rs 70,051 crore in health grants through local governments for FY2021-22 to FY2025-26.{{2}} States decide whether to join Union schemes: Odisha and Delhi adopted PM-JAY in 2025, and West Bengal's entry in June 2026 completed nationwide rollout.{{3}}{{4}}{{5}} Several states also finance their own health insurance schemes.{{8}} For a foreign partner, the counterparty is often a state government; Cleveland Clinic's June 2026 MediCity MoU, for example, was signed with the Government of Maharashtra.{{6}}

financing.narrative:
The National Health Accounts for 2022-23 put total health expenditure at 3.37 percent of GDP, or Rs 6,373 per person, and government spending at 1.48 percent, both on the new GDP series; on the old 2011-12 series the ratios are 3.28 and 1.43 percent.{{1}}{{2}}{{3}}{{4}} Government spending is well short of the 2.5 percent target for 2025 set by the National Health Policy 2017.{{9}}

From 2013-14 to 2022-23 the government share of total health spending rose from 28.6 to 43.7 percent, and the out-of-pocket share fell from 64.2 to 43.4 percent.{{2}} The out-of-pocket share had been 39.4 percent in COVID-affected 2021-22, and households paid more again once emergency spending ended.{{5}}{{2}}{{3}} Health insurance coverage reached 47.4 percent in rural and 44.3 percent in urban areas in 2025, up from 14.1 and 19.1 percent in 2017-18, yet out-of-pocket spending still averaged Rs 34,064 per hospitalisation, excluding childbirth.{{7}}{{8}} For a foreign partner, this means a two-tier market: a mass market anchored by PM-JAY rates and a smaller cash-paying, privately insured and international segment that sustains premium tertiary care.

workforce.narrative:
India's health workforce remains thin: it had 13.88 lakh registered allopathic doctors in December 2025, fewer than one per 1,000 people, and fewer still practise.{{1}}{{3}} The official ratio of one doctor per 811 people counts 7.5 lakh AYUSH practitioners and assumes 80 percent of registrants are active.{{1}}{{3}} India had 46.02 lakh registered nursing personnel at 31 December 2025, or 2.60 per 1,000, but only 14.24 lakh were enrolled in the Nurses Registration and Tracking System in 2026, so the number working in India is uncertain.{{4}}{{5}}

India is below WHO's threshold of 4.45 doctors, nurses and midwives per 1,000 and far below OECD averages of roughly 4 doctors and 9 nurses per 1,000 reported in 2025.{{4}}{{7}}{{8}}{{9}} Shortages are worst in the northern states, and rural community health centres lacked 79.9 percent of their required specialists in March 2023.{{4}}{{15}} The Union Budget 2026-27 plans to add 1 lakh allied health professionals over five years and train 1.5 lakh caregivers.{{11}}{{12}}{{13}} For a foreign academic partner, workforce development, from nursing programs and fellowships to allied-health and leadership training, is one of the clearest openings.

competitive_landscape.narrative: Leading US academic systems work in India mainly through advisory, network, second-opinion and education models rather than ownership, and several announced relationships are older or less visible than their headlines suggest. Foreign capital, by contrast, comes mainly from an Asian strategic owner and global private equity backing Indian hospital chains.{{31}}{{37}}{{40}}

entries.text: AIG Hospitals joined the Mayo Clinic Care Network in October 2019, and Mayo's 2023 tax filings still listed India among member locations.{{1}}{{2}}{{3}} Lilavati announced a nursing program, a 300-bed cancer institute and a GIFT City project with Mayo in January 2025, and trained 120 nurses in March 2025.{{6}}{{7}} Adani engaged Mayo in February 2025 to advise on two Health City campuses.{{5}} Mayo opened a patient information office in Mumbai in February 2023.{{4}}

entries.text: UCLA's OB/GYN department launched a resident exchange with Narendra Modi Medical College in 2024, began joint academic seminars in summer 2025 and completed the first phase of a postpartum-haemorrhage quality project with AIIMS New Delhi.{{18}} These are grant-funded departmental projects, not UCLA Health system affiliations.{{18}}

entries.partner: Emergency services in Ahmedabad and Mumbai
entries.status: Held 2007 and 2008; no current program publicly listed
entries.text: NewYork-Presbyterian emergency-medicine volunteers ran disaster-preparedness training and drills in Ahmedabad in November 2007 and in Mumbai in October and November 2008.{{23}}

entries.model: Telemedicine second opinions; clinical pathology laboratory development
entries.status: Announced 2014; current status not confirmed; India not listed on UPMC International's locations page (2026)
entries.text: UPMC signed a telemedicine second-opinion agreement with TeleChikitsa Ventures in February 2014, its second India agreement after helping Citizens Hospital build a clinical pathology laboratory.{{24}} UPMC International's locations page lists Croatia, Ireland and Italy but not India.{{25}}

entries.model: Hospital development, clinical programs and quality improvement, through Harvard Medical International and later Partners Harvard Medical International
entries.status: Began about 2001; current status not confirmed; no India partnership on MGB's global partnerships page (2026)
entries.text: Harvard Medical International helped Wockhardt Hospitals develop facilities, clinical programs and a performance-improvement plan that led to international accreditation.{{26}} Partners HealthCare took over HMI in 2008 as Partners Harvard Medical International and announced in November 2019 that it would rename itself Mass General Brigham.{{38}}{{39}} Wockhardt described a ten-year PHMI relationship in 2010-11, and MGB's global partnerships page does not list India.{{27}}{{28}}
No India partnership was found on the international pages of Houston Methodist or Northwestern Medicine.{{29}}{{30}}

entries.group: Other foreign health systems and investors
entries.status: Controlling shareholder; open offer closed November 2025
entries.text: Malaysia's IHH Healthcare controls Fortis.{{31}} Its mandatory open offer closed in November 2025 with only 1,778 shares tendered, leaving its stake at about 31.17 percent.{{31}}

entries.group: Other foreign health systems and investors
entries.partner: Aster DM Quality Care (Aster DM Healthcare merged with Quality Care India)
entries.text: Aster DM Healthcare and Blackstone-backed Quality Care India announced their merger in January 2025, and the combined Aster DM Quality Care began operating in July 2026 with more than 10,600 beds.{{37}}{{41}}

entries.group: Other foreign health systems and investors
entries.status: Agreed August 2026; closing expected in the fourth quarter of 2026
entries.text: KKR agreed on 6 August 2026 to buy Medicover India, 24 hospitals with about 4,800 beds, from Sweden's Medicover, which is leaving the Indian hospital market.{{40}}{{32}} Closing is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to approvals.{{32}}

entries.group: Other foreign health systems and investors
entries.institution: King's College London; Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
entries.status: Formed April 2024; current status not confirmed
entries.text: King's College London and Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust formed a Health Partners Academy with P. D. Hinduja Hospital in April 2024.{{33}}{{34}}

competitive_landscape.closing: India also competes for international patients. Medical-purpose arrivals were 6.44 lakh in 2024, led by Bangladesh with about 4.8 lakh, followed by Iraq, Somalia, Oman and Uzbekistan.{{35}}{{36}} Indian chains market lower-cost complex care to the same Gulf, African and Central Asian patients that US centers pursue, and the Union Budget 2026-27 backs five regional medical hubs to strengthen that position.{{35}}{{36}}{{42}}

recent_developments.headline: Union Budget 2026-27 raises health allocation nearly 10% and backs five regional medical hubs
recent_developments.summary: The Health Ministry received Rs 1,06,530.42 crore, nearly 10 percent above the previous year's revised estimate, including Rs 39,390 crore for the National Health Mission and Rs 9,500 crore for PM-JAY.{{1}} The budget also backed five regional medical hubs and plans to add 1 lakh allied health professionals and train 1.5 lakh caregivers.{{1}}{{2}}

recent_developments.headline: NEET-UG 2026 cancelled over alleged paper leak; re-examination held on 21 June
recent_developments.summary: The National Testing Agency cancelled the 3 May 2026 NEET-UG examination on 12 May over alleged irregularities, including a reported paper leak, and the government referred the case to the CBI.{{1}}{{4}} Close to 20 lakh candidates sat the re-examination on 21 June, and 11.21 lakh qualified when results were declared on 16 July 2026.{{2}}{{3}}

resolution_log: MSK and iCliniq: removed the claim that the MSK India pages remain live. Every mskcc.icliniq.com URL now returns HTTP 410 ('permanently removed'), which I confirmed myself. The text now states the confirmed 2 August 2021 launch (PR Newswire release, opened) and says current status is unknown and the program may have ended. Raised by V1+V2+V3.

GDP (PPP): replaced the stale US$16.2 trillion and US$11,159 per capita (2024) with the current World Bank series, US$17.2 trillion and US$11,748 per capita for 2025, keeping 2024 values of US$15.6 trillion and US$10,719. I queried the World Bank API myself (last updated 13 July 2026). Removed the Trading Economics source. Raised by V1+V2+V3.

Urban population: corrected 36.9% (2024) to 35.7% (2025), with 35.4% for 2024, per the World Bank API, which I queried myself. The narrative's 'about 37 percent' became 'about 36 percent in 2025'. Raised by V1+V2+V3.

Johns Hopkins and IIT Bombay: corrected the agreement year from 2025 to 9 February 2023. The '2025' came from the page's URL folder. JHU sites block automated fetches, so I confirmed the date through the institute's indexed pages, and all three verifiers agree. Raised by V1+V2+V3.

US tariffs: rewrote the sequence. Trump announced the deal on 2 February 2026; the joint statement is dated 6 February (White House, opened). The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs on 20 February (Akashvani, opened), a 10% Section 122 tariff followed from 24 February, and a 10% Section 301 duty has applied to India since 24 July 2026 (Morgan Lewis, opened). The Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act was signed on 18 September 2026 (Baker McKenzie, opened). The verifiers' correct versions differed on the current regime; I adopted V3's Section 301 version after confirming it. Raised by V1+V2+V3.

Mayo and AIG: V1 said membership was 'probably active', while V2 and V3 could not check it. I confirmed the October 2019 joining (Mayo release on Newswise) and that the Post Bulletin (February 2025) cites 2023 tax filings listing India among member locations. AIG's own Mayo page returns 404 and Mayo's member list blocks fetches. The text now states what is confirmed and says present membership is not confirmed, without calling it active. Raised by V1.

Mayo and Lilavati: widened the scope from nursing alone to the January 2025 announcement, which also covered a 300-bed cancer institute and a GIFT City project (Medical Buyer/PTI, opened). Removed the past tense 'ran'. The text says those projects are described only by Lilavati's trustees, that Mayo did not answer press questions (Post Bulletin, opened), and that their status is unknown. Raised by V1.

Mayo and Adani: removed the 'strictly advisory, not a joint venture' spokesperson quote. It appears only in a Star Tribune search snippet, and the article could not be opened. Mayo's role is now described from Adani's own 10 February 2025 release, which I opened. Found in my own check.

Mayo Mumbai office: removed the unsupported word 'active'. The office is now dated to its February 2023 opening (Mayo release on Newswise, opened), and the Mumbai subsidiary named in Mayo's filings was added. Found in my own check.

Max Healthcare: corrected 5,257 operational beds to 4,966 at 31 March 2026 (Business Standard, InvestyWise), plus the 10,000-bed FY2030 target. The cited Whalesbook source never gave 5,257. Raised by V1.

MD Anderson and Tata Memorial: replaced 'current formal status is not confirmed'. MD Anderson's own ECHO-PACA II page, which I opened, lists Tata Memorial Hospital under a Sister Institution Network Fund grant. Confirmed the 6 October 2003 signing (India Herald, opened). Dropped the SACT 2025 joint-session reference because the only source is a December 2024 social post announcing it. Raised by V2; V1 and V3 had it in could_not_check.

UPMC: changed 'historical' to 'no current India activity found', since absence from a location list does not show the agreement ended. Added the earlier Citizens Hospital, Hyderabad pathology-lab work. Checked against the EurekAlert release and the UPMC locations page, both opened. Raised by V2.
NewYork-Presbyterian: added dates, Ahmedabad in November 2007 and Mumbai from October to November 2008, from the NYP release, which I opened. Raised by V1+V2.

UCLA: reframed as department-level, grant-funded OB/GYN (GRACE) projects: the Narendra Modi Medical College exchange (2024 pilot, seminars from summer 2025) and the completed first phase of the AIIMS postpartum-haemorrhage project. Confirmed on UCLA's page, which I opened. Raised by V1.

Mount Sinai and Ramaiah: added the omitted July 2024 exclusive long-term collaboration. Confirmed with Mount Sinai Press Office's GlobeNewswire release of 12 July 2024 (opened via Yahoo Finance), Deccan Herald on the 10-year term from 1 July 2024 (opened), and Ramaiah's collaborations page, which still presents the partnership (opened). Current activity is not asserted beyond that. Raised by V3.

Johns Hopkins and HCL: no verifier could check this. JHMI's own page, via its indexed text, describes a 10-year affiliation from February 2014, and a 2014 Domain-b report (opened) confirms the tie-up. The text states the term would have ended in 2024 and that no renewal or current activity could be confirmed. From the could_not_check lists of V1+V2+V3.

Cleveland Clinic MediCity: confirmed the 10 June 2026 MoU, the parties, the 250 acres, US$1.2 billion and 10,000 jobs, and the Mihaljevic quote through the state's announcement as carried by Free Press Journal and India TV, both opened. Cleveland Clinic's newsroom has no release, so the text now says so. Confirmed the in-country representative on Cleveland Clinic's India page. Found in my own check.

NCD premature mortality: corrected 22% (2019) to 23.6% (2021), with 23.7% for 2019, from the WHO Global Health Observatory API (NCDMORT3070), which I queried myself. Updated the narrative to match. Raised by V3.

SRS indicators: updated to the SRS Statistical Report 2024 (released May 2026): TFR 1.9 (2024), IMR 24 (2024), Bihar 2.9 and Delhi 1.2. Replaced '18 states and UTs below 2.1' with 'all states except six in the north', per The Wire and Business Standard, both opened. Raised by V2+V3.

National Health Accounts: made the GDP series consistent. THE is 3.37% on the new series and 3.28% on the old; GHE is 1.48% on the new series and 1.43% on the old. I checked this against the NHA 2022-23 report text. Raised by V2+V3.

Government hospital beds: the three verifiers disagreed. V1 attributed the 0.79 figure to Knight Frank, V2 to National Health Profile data, and V3 to beds as of 31 March 2021. I opened the source chain: Knight Frank's number is actually a 1.3 total-bed ratio, and the official figure is 8,18,661 public beds as of 31 March 2023 (PIB Rajya Sabha reply, Health Dynamics of India 2022-23). That works out to fewer than 0.6 per 1,000, and the 0.79 figure cannot be reproduced from official data. Replaced it with the official count and removed the unsourced '2.7 global average'. Raised by V1+V2+V3.

Postgraduate seats: added the official 82,059 total that the Health Minister gave Parliament in December 2025 (Deccan Herald, opened), with the roughly 57,500 NMC matrix figure presented as a narrower MD/MS count. Raised by V1+V2.

NEET-UG 2026: added the cancellation of the 3 May sitting on 12 May over a paper leak, the CBI probe, and the fact that 21 June was a re-examination. Confirmed on Wikipedia and in the NTA result notice. Added a matching recent-development entry. Raised by V1+V3.
Pharma exports: changed 'about a third to the US' to about US$9.5 billion (roughly 30%), down nearly 10% year on year, with a total of US$31.1 billion (Business Standard, opened). Raised by V1.
GDP: added Q1 FY2026-27 real growth of 7.8% from the MoSPI press note of 31 August 2026, which I opened. Raised by V2.

West Bengal PM-JAY: split the families into 1.24 crore eligible and about 1.43 crore including ASHA, anganwadi and 70+ families (PIB, opened). Removed the unconfirmed Vigyan Bhavan venue. Raised by V2+V3; V1 had the venue in could_not_check.
Out-of-pocket costs: added the 'excluding childbirth' qualifier and the private-hospital average of Rs 50,508 (median Rs 24,000 against Rs 1,100), from the NSS press note text. Raised by V2.

IHH and Fortis: corrected the implication that the open offer raised IHH's stake. IHH has held about 31.17% since 2018, and only 1,778 shares were tendered (InvestyWise BSE summary, opened). Raised by V2+V3.

KKR and Medicover: attributed the EUR 1.2 billion (about US$1.4 billion) valuation and Q4 2026 closing to Medicover's own release, which I opened, and noted that KKR did not disclose terms. Raised by V2+V3.

Medical arrivals: changed 'reached 6.44 lakh' to show the decline from 6.59 lakh (2023) and 6.97 lakh (2019) (DD News, opened). Confirmed the 2024 source-country ranking led by Bangladesh at about 4.8 lakh via InsightsIAS, citing Bureau of Immigration data. Raised by V3; the ranking was in the could_not_check lists of V1+V2+V3.

MBBS seats: dated the matrix to September 2026. Replaced the unverified 2024 baseline of 1,17,750 with the official 1,28,875 UG seats reported to Parliament in December 2025. Did not add V3's 'excludes INIs' point because the source I opened does not state it. Raised by V3; the baseline was in V2's could_not_check.

Gujarat private admissions (60 to 65%): removed. The only source (Counterview) is internally inconsistent and says the all-India shares are identical to Gujarat's. Replaced with the NSS private and public cost comparison. From the could_not_check lists of V1+V2+V3.

Manipal IPO: removed 'second-largest Indian IPO of 2026', which is unsupported, and changed 4.92 times to 'nearly five times' per Business Standard. Added the 33-hospital 2024 baseline from Groww's DRHP summary. From V3's could_not_check.

NExT: replaced 'expected around 2028 to 2029' with the October 2025 NMC statement of no implementation for three to four years while mock tests run (Medical Dialogues, opened). From the could_not_check lists of V2+V3.
NRTS enrolment of 14.24 lakh: confirmed via August 2026 reporting of Lok Sabha data (Chennai Online, opened) and added the source. From the could_not_check lists of V1+V2+V3.

EY-Parthenon pipelines and Medanta beds: confirmed Apollo about 3,400 (FY2027 to FY2030), Medanta about 2,700 and Fortis about 1,800 in Business Standard's coverage of the EY report, and added Aster's roughly 4,445. Confirmed Medanta's 3,665 beds, consistent with its 623-bed FY2026 addition. From the could_not_check lists of V2+V3.

OECD comparators: the OECD pages block fetches, so I rounded to 'roughly 4 doctors, 9.2 nurses and just over 4 beds' to match indexed OECD text (3.9, 9.2 and 4.2). From the could_not_check lists of V1+V2.
Narayana Health: corrected the UK acquisition date from November to October 2025, per Narayana's own release dated 31 October 2025. Found in my own check.

Apollo: corrected the bed-base description from 'owned, managed and affiliated' to owned and managed hospitals plus day-surgery and cradle units in India and overseas, per the Q4 FY26 release text. Found in my own check.
Aster DM Quality Care: added '28 cities' and confirmed 39 hospitals and more than 10,600 beds (HealthCare Middle East and Africa, opened). From V2's could_not_check.

Houston Methodist, Northwestern and MGB: rephrased the absence claim as 'no India hospital partnership found on their international pages', after checking each page. Partners Harvard Medical International and Wockhardt were confirmed via Wockhardt's 2010-11 annual report ('ten year relationship'). Found in my own check.
